summary: The bill designates the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission as the sole lead agency for NEPA reviews of natural gas pipeline projects under the Natural Gas Act, requires it to coordinate early with other agencies and set binding schedules, and bars non-participating agencies from conducting their own supplemental reviews or water-quality certifications.

scores.thoughts: The bill addresses interagency coordination and timelines for pipeline permitting under the Natural Gas Act and NEPA. It contains no provisions related to federal appropriations, budgets, or expenditures.
The bill makes no changes to tax law, rates, credits, or revenue collection.
No provisions address healthcare policy, insurance, or medical services.
The legislation is unrelated to firearms regulation or Second Amendment issues.
No content pertains to immigration, visas, or border policy.
The bill contains nothing related to reproductive rights or abortion access.
No provisions affect military budgets, defense programs, or national security spending.

The bill centralizes NEPA review authority with FERC for natural gas pipelines, limits supplemental environmental reviews by other agencies, removes the requirement for section 401 water quality certifications, and imposes strict deadlines on permitting. These changes expedite fossil-fuel infrastructure approvals and reduce the scope of environmental oversight, thereby limiting environmental regulations.
